title: Water-Filled Acoustic Impedance Tubes and Two-Layer Material Specimens: Geometry Design, Sample Sizing and Transfer-Matrix Method in Underwater Conditions
content: The paper presents an integrated methodology for designing water-filled acoustic impedance tubes and interpreting measurements of the acoustic impedance of single- and multilayer polymer and elastomer in underwater conditions. The first part consolidates a family concept of three circular, water-filled tubes dedicated to different frequencies, respectively, based on a plane-wave criterion, wall-stiffness constraints and a four-hydrophone configuration with two end-cap sensors and two mid-span sensors positioned symmetrically around the sample. The proposed geometry sizing algorithm derives tube length, inner diameter, wall thickness, tube material selection and deaeration requirements for the laboratory stand. The second part links the hardware proposal to the physics requirements in water by recalling the relations between sound pressure, par-ticle velocity and specific impedance. Moreover, there is a proposal for formulating reflection, transmission and absorption coefficients for normal incidence at water–solid plates. Using a Transfer-Matrix Method (TMM), single-layer and multilayer configurations such as water–elastomer–water and water–rubber–polymer–water are modelled with complex wavenumbers to account for frequency-dependent phase velocity and attenuation. This approach enables prediction of resonance bands and broadband absorption behaviour in the 10–100 kHz range.
